newsitem.title: UK: GiroVend shares set debut premium.
newsitem.headline: GiroVend shares set debut premium.

text.p: Shares in GiroVend Plc, a supplier of cashless payment systems, set a premium on their first day of trade on the London Stock Exchange on Thursday.
By 1110 GMT, the shares were quoted at 178-1/2p, ahead of the 160p issue price, with 880,736 shares traded.
GiroVend said it raised a net 7.0 million stg, with a pre-float placing valuing it at 20.8 million stg.
The proceeds from the float will be used to cut borrowing and increase working capital, GiroVend said.
GiroVend designs, assembles and supplies stored value card payment systems to a wide range of clients.
The company said its systems were generally used in in-house catering and vending, eliminating the need for cash in the work-place.
Its major customers include Marks & Spencer, J Sainsbury, BMW AG, Nissan Motor Manufacture UK 7201.t, British Airways, General Accident, Morgan Grenfell and Arthur Andersen.

GiroVend, originally set up in Germany in 1979 as Mico-Datensysteme GmBH, said had it recently entered into a cooperation agreement with Mondex, the "electronic purse" developer, which has taken a ten percent stake in GiroVend.
The broker and sponsor to the issue was Collins Stewart.
